plan.topic: Do tirzepatide and other GLP-1 medicines affect mood or anxiety? New neuropsychiatric safety review (Rambam Maimonides Med J, Oct 26, 2026), the Medicare cohort (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 25), and a semaglutide panic-attack pharmacovigilance study with a notoriety-bias check (Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf, Nov 2026)
plan.angle: Calm 'honest uncertainty' Short built on two anchors. (1) FDA Drug Safety Communication, 13 Jan 2026 (https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-communications/fda-requests-removal-suicidal-behavior-and-ideation-warning-glucagon-peptide-1-receptor-agonist-glp): the FDA asked for the suicidal-thoughts warning to be removed from the Zepbound, Wegovy and Saxenda labels after its review of 91 placebo-controlled trials found no increased risk of suicidal thoughts or other psychiatric side effects. (2) The Oct 2026 Rambam review, which covers GLP-1 medicines and tirzepatide, using its conclusion wording verbatim. Optional third line, only if words allow: a semaglutide panic-attack reporting study found that reports jumped after 2023 media and regulatory attention, which is consistent with notoriety bias, so a reporting signal isn't proof of cause. Label it semaglutide and FAERS. Drop the Medicare cohort unless content_check confirms its findings and drug scope. Required lines: 'Everyone's different. If your mood changes on any medicine, tell your prescriber.' The crisis line: 988 in the US, Samaritans 116 123 in the UK, or local emergency services. 'Don't stop or change your medicines on your own.' 'Not personal advice.' Plus the full prescriber line. Title: 'Tirzepatide and Mood: What the Evidence Shows'. No #semaglutide unless the panic-attack line stays, and no emoji.

plan.why: Body-worry honest-uncertainty format (proven, median ~104), tirzepatide-first title, three fresh papers within a week, and low competition from calm sources. Brain topic adds body-system variety. | fact-check: All three cited sources exist. (a) Jani et al., 'Neuropsychiatric Safety of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Tirzepatide in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus or Obesity', Rambam Maimonides Med J 17(4), Oct 2026, https://www.rmmj.org.il/issues/73/articles/4883. I couldn't retrieve the conclusion text, so content_check must quote it from the PDF. (b) Baik et al., Diabetes Obes Metab, Medicare beneficiaries with type 2 diabetes, observational, https://dom-pubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/dom.71459. The publisher returned 403, so confirm the findings and whether tirzepatide was even included. If it wasn't, call it 'GLP-1 medicines' only. (c) Melamed et al., Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf 2026, https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/pds.70517. FAERS 2018Q1–2024Q4, active comparators dulaglutide and empagliflozin. The crude semaglutide–panic attack signal weakened after adjustment, was not significant before the July 2023 regulatory communication, then rose in a pattern consistent with notoriety bias. Problems: three studies, a crisis line and three safety lines won't fit in 170 words. More importantly, the angle leaves out the strongest, most relevant dated fact. On 13 Jan 2026 the FDA asked for the suicidal behaviour and ideation warning to be removed from the Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound labels after a review found no increased risk (a meta-analysis of 91 placebo-controlled trials, 107,901 patients). The tone must stay 'honest uncertainty', not 'all clear'. Individual mood changes still matter and should be reported.

social.instagram_caption:
Worried tirzepatide, semaglutide or other GLP-1 medicines could affect your mood? Here's what the FDA's safety review found, and why a reporting signal may mislead.

In January 2026, the FDA asked to remove the suicidal-thoughts warning from tirzepatide (Zepbound), semaglutide (Wegovy) and liraglutide (Saxenda). After reviewing 91 placebo-controlled GLP-1 trials, it found no increased risk of suicidal thoughts, depression or anxiety.

A separate pharmacovigilance study on semaglutide found a panic-attack reporting signal that shrank once researchers adjusted for who's prescribed it. The signal wasn't significant before mid-2023, when regulators started reviewing. Then reports jumped. That pattern fits notoriety bias: news coverage drives more reports.

A safety report isn't proof of a side effect, and results can differ person to person.

Save this to bring to your next prescriber visit.

Everyone's different: if your mood changes on any medicine, tell your prescriber. In crisis: 988 (US/Canada), Samaritans 116 123 (UK), Lifeline 13 11 14 (Australia), or local emergency services. Don't stop or change your medicines on your own.

factcheck.summary: Both sources are real and the script matches them. FDA Drug Safety Communication, 13 Jan 2026: FDA asked for the suicidal behavior and ideation warning to be removed from Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound. Its meta-analysis covered 91 placebo-controlled GLP-1 RA trials (107,910 people) and found no increased risk of SI/B, anxiety, depression, irritability or psychosis. Melamed et al. (2026, Pharmacoepidemiology and Drug Safety) reports a crude FAERS semaglutide–panic-attack signal that "attenuated after adjustment" (age, sex, indication). It "was no longer significant before the July 2023 regulatory communication and rose sharply thereafter in a pattern consistent with notoriety bias". The script keeps the class-study framing ("GLP-1 trials"), labels the panic-attack data as semaglutide-only, and hedges well ("Reassuring, not guaranteed"). It carries crisis lines, the don't-stop line, "Not personal advice" and the prescriber line. Narration is about 168 words, under the 170 cap. The fixes below are small precision edits: the July 2023 review was by the EMA (European regulators), and the paper says the pattern is "consistent with" notoriety bias, not that coverage proven to drive reports. Note: the Wiley page returns 403 to automated fetches but the article is confirmed in search; use the PubMed record if the publisher can find the PMID.

issues.claim: And it wasn't significant before mid twenty twenty-three, when regulators started reviewing.
issues.problem: The July 2023 review that Melamed uses as the cut-off was the EMA PRAC investigation, not an FDA review. Right after 'In FDA side-effect reports', plain 'regulators' suggests it was the FDA.
issues.fix: And it wasn't significant before July twenty twenty-three, when European regulators started reviewing.

issues.claim: That fits notoriety bias: news coverage drives more reports.
issues.problem: The paper says the pattern is 'consistent with' notoriety bias. Saying coverage 'drives' more reports states the mechanism as fact.
issues.fix: That fits notoriety bias: publicity can drive more reports.

issues.claim: reports rose after regulators began reviewing
issues.problem: Same attribution issue: it was the EMA's July 2023 review.
issues.fix: Semaglutide panic-attack reports (FAERS): after adjustment, no significant signal in reports filed before the July 2023 EMA review; reports rose sharply after

issues.claim: the FDA asked to remove the suicidal-thoughts warning from tirzepatide's Zepbound, plus Wegovy and Saxenda
issues.problem: The FDA asked the drugmakers to remove the warning. The current wording leaves unclear who was asked and could sound like the FDA removed it itself.
issues.fix: In January twenty twenty-six, the FDA asked drugmakers to remove the suicidal-thoughts warning from tirzepatide's Zepbound, plus Wegovy and Saxenda.

audio.soundNotes: Music sits right in the target window under voice (-13.5dB) but was a bit hot in pauses (-12.3 vs ~-14 target), so pulled overall gain to 0.85. Thinned redundant simultaneous SFX (duplicate bubbles at the whip transition, extra swooshes/whoosh/tick stacked at the 91-trials reveal, the 52s and 56s swoosh clusters, and the closing swoosh pile-up) to stay under the 3–4-per-second rule and keep the serious "Reports aren't proof" and closing disclaimer beats uncluttered. Pulled down two SFX that were too loud over speech (blip at 6.4s, pop at 18.7s, both now in the -14 to -20dB felt range) while leaving the two pause-timed reveal swells/dings (17.8s, 59.3s, 72.1s) at their punchier -6 to -9dB since they land in silence. Added five bespoke, restrained accents (document stamp, file flutter, tension-release piano note, a felt heartbeat pulse on the 988 stat, and a warm closing chime) to give the FDA-label and reports-aren't-proof beats a distinct, non-generic texture without competing with narration.
